summary.title: Your First Machine Learning Project in Python Step-By-Step
summary.one_liner: You learn to run a complete beginner machine learning project in Python, from installing SciPy libraries through loading, summarizing and visualizing the iris dataset to comparing six classifiers with cross-validation.
keywords: box and whisker plot algorithm comparison
logistic regression lda knn cart naive bayes svm
how to start machine learning in python
takeaways: Check that the Python, SciPy, numpy, matplotlib, pandas and scikit-learn environment works before starting (tutorial assumes Python 3.6+ and scikit-learn 0.20+).
Load the iris CSV with pandas, then inspect it with shape, head, describe and groupby class counts.
Use box plots, histograms and a scatter matrix to understand attribute distributions and relationships.
Hold out 20% as a validation set, then compare six models with stratified 10-fold cross-validation on accuracy; SVM scored highest (about 0.98) in the author's run.
Follow the five-step project template (define, prepare, evaluate, improve, present) on other datasets.
summary.summary: This tutorial walks a beginner through a complete small machine learning project in Python using the iris flower dataset. It covers installing and checking the SciPy-stack libraries, loading data from a URL with pandas, and summarizing it with statistics and class counts. It then shows univariate and multivariate plots, creates a validation split, and compares six scikit-learn classifiers (LR, LDA, KNN, CART, NB, SVM) with stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The page ends by choosing the SVM as the final model and starting to check it on the held-out validation set; the cut-off text does not include those final results.
